q:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

Trees in cities do far more than make streets look pleasant. Their leaves absorb pollutants and trap dust, improving the air that residents breathe. In summer, their shade can lower the temperature of streets and buildings by several degrees, which reduces the need for air conditioning. Their roots take in rainwater and so lessen the risk of flooding after heavy storms. Trees also soften the noise of traffic and give birds and insects a place to live in the middle of concrete and glass. Some studies even suggest that people who live near green spaces report lower levels of stress. For these reasons, many city governments no longer treat trees as decoration. They count them, map them, and budget for their care in the same way as they do for roads, pipes, and other essential public facilities.
opts: difficulties of growing trees in crowded cities
ways to cut the cost of air conditioning
various benefits that trees bring to cities
major causes of flooding in urban areas
exp: 도시의 나무가 공기를 맑게 하고, 기온을 낮추고, 홍수 위험과 소음을 줄이고, 스트레스를 덜어 준다는 여러 이점을 나열한 뒤, 그래서 시 정부가 나무를 필수 공공시설처럼 관리한다고 맺는 글이다. 냉방과 홍수는 이점의 예로 잠깐 나올 뿐이고, 나무를 기르기 어렵다는 내용은 없다.

q:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

Government documents are often filled with long sentences and technical terms that ordinary citizens find hard to follow. When people cannot understand a notice, they may miss a deadline, fill out a form incorrectly, or fail to receive a benefit they are entitled to. Offices then have to spend time answering the same questions by phone again and again, and mistakes on forms must be corrected one by one. For this reason, a growing number of public agencies are training their employees to write in plain language: short sentences, familiar words, and the most important point first. Some agencies also test a draft on a few members of the public before sending it out, to see whether readers can find what they need. Clear writing is not a matter of style alone. It saves time and money for both the public and the government.
opts: how citizens can apply for government benefits
the long history of government record keeping
the difficulty of learning technical terms
the need for plain language in public documents
exp: 공문서가 어려우면 시민은 기한을 놓치거나 혜택을 받지 못하고 기관은 같은 문의와 서류 수정에 시간을 쓰게 되므로, 짧은 문장과 익숙한 낱말로 쉽게 써야 한다는 글이다. 혜택은 피해의 예로 나올 뿐 신청 방법을 설명하지 않고, 기록 관리의 역사나 전문 용어를 배우는 어려움은 다루지 않는다.

q:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

In many countries the number of elderly people living alone is rising rapidly. Living alone is not a problem in itself, and many older people value their independence. It can become dangerous, however, when no one notices that a person has fallen ill, has had a fall, or has stopped eating properly. Some local governments have responded by asking mail carriers, meter readers, and delivery workers to report anything unusual at the homes they visit regularly, such as uncollected mail or lights left on all day. Others have installed sensors that send an alert to a care worker when there has been no movement in a home for many hours. In some neighborhoods, volunteers telephone older residents every morning simply to ask how they are. Each of these measures aims at the same thing: making sure that help arrives before a small problem turns into a tragedy.
opts: reasons why elderly people prefer to live alone
poor working conditions of delivery workers
efforts to watch over elderly people living alone
privacy problems caused by sensors in homes
exp: 혼자 사는 노인이 늘어나자 집배원과 검침원의 신고, 움직임 감지 장치, 자원봉사자의 안부 전화 같은 방법으로 이들을 살피려 한다는 글이다. 마지막 문장이 이 조치들의 공통된 목적(문제가 커지기 전에 도움이 닿게 함)을 정리한다. 혼자 사는 이유, 배달 노동자의 근무 여건, 감지 장치의 사생활 문제는 언급되지 않는다.

q:

In most cities, the budget is drawn up by officials and approved by the council, and residents learn about it only afterward. Some local governments, however, now set aside part of the budget for residents to decide. Neighbors gather to propose projects, such as repairing a playground or adding streetlights on a dark road. Officials then estimate the cost of each proposal, and residents vote on which ones should be funded. Supporters say the process directs money to needs that officials, who cannot walk every street, might never notice. It also gives residents a better understanding of how public money is spent and a stronger sense that the city belongs to them. Critics point out that the amounts involved are usually small and that people with free time are more likely to take part. Even so, the number of cities trying the approach continues to grow.
opts: reasons for the rising cost of public facilities
ways to reduce crime on dark streets
conflicts between officials and city councils
letting residents decide how part of the budget is spent
exp: 예산의 일부를 주민이 직접 제안하고 투표로 정하게 하는 제도와 그 장점, 한계를 설명한 글이다. 가로등은 주민이 제안하는 사업의 예로 나올 뿐이고, 공공시설 비용의 증가나 공무원과 의회의 갈등은 언급되지 않는다.

q:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water, and they need very little of it. A flowerpot saucer, an old tire, or a blocked gutter can produce hundreds of insects in a short time during warm weather. This is why health authorities, when they try to control diseases carried by mosquitoes, ask residents to do more than spray insecticide. Spraying kills only the adults that happen to be flying at the time, and new ones soon take their place. Emptying containers after rain, covering water tanks, and clearing drains, on the other hand, remove the places where the insects breed. Because a mosquito can grow from egg to adult in little more than a week in hot weather, this needs to be done regularly rather than once a season. A neighborhood that leaves no standing water stops the next generation from ever appearing, which no amount of spraying can achieve.
opts: the health risks of using insecticide at home
the reasons mosquitoes prefer warm weather
the proper way to water flowerpots
the need to remove standing water to control mosquitoes
exp: 모기는 고인 물에 알을 낳으므로, 날아다니는 성충만 죽이는 살충제보다 고인 물을 없애는 것이 다음 세대의 모기를 막는 길이라는 글이다. 살충제가 건강에 해롭다는 말은 없고, 화분 받침은 모기가 생기는 곳의 예일 뿐이며, 더운 날씨는 모기가 빨리 자라는 조건으로만 나온다.

q:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

A large share of the food thrown away at home is still perfectly safe to eat. One reason is confusion about the dates printed on packages. Many shoppers assume that food becomes harmful the day after a "sell-by" date. This date, however, is only a guide for stores, telling them how long a product may stay on the shelf, and it says little about safety. Properly stored milk, eggs, and bread usually remain good for days beyond it. Yet people who are unsure tend to play it safe and put the food in the trash. To reduce such waste, some countries have replaced the sell-by date with a "use-by" date, which tells consumers how long a product can actually be eaten if it is stored as directed. A clearer label, it is hoped, will keep good food out of the garbage.
opts: How to Store Milk and Eggs at Home
Why Fresh Food Costs More Than Before
The Dangers of Eating Expired Food
Misunderstood Date Labels and Food Waste
exp: 포장에 적힌 판매 기한을 먹을 수 있는 기한으로 오해해서 멀쩡한 음식을 버리게 되고, 이를 줄이려고 표시를 바꾸는 나라가 있다는 글이다. 기한이 지난 음식이 위험하다는 것은 글이 바로잡으려는 오해이고, 보관 방법이나 식품 가격은 중심 내용이 아니다.

q:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

People usually volunteer in order to help others, but those who give their time often gain as much as they give. Serving meals at a shelter or reading to children in a hospital brings volunteers into contact with people they would otherwise never meet, and many form lasting friendships. Retired people in particular say that regular volunteer work gives their week a structure and a sense of purpose that they missed after leaving their jobs. Volunteers also pick up practical skills, from organizing events to speaking in public, that prove useful in their own careers. For young people who have not yet held a job, such experience can be a first chance to work in a team and to be relied on by others. None of this is the reason most people sign up. Still, helping others, it turns out, is also a way of helping oneself.
opts: The Decline of Volunteering among the Young
exp: 봉사자는 남을 돕는 동안 새로운 사람들과의 우정, 삶의 목적의식, 실용적인 기술과 협동의 경험을 얻는다는 글이다. 마지막 문장이 "남을 돕는 것은 자신을 돕는 길"이라고 정리한다. 봉사자 모집 방법, 쉼터에 대한 정부 지원, 청년 봉사의 감소는 다루지 않는다.

q:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

For most of human history, the night sky was filled with thousands of stars. Today, people living in large cities can see only a handful, because the glow of streetlights and signs washes out the rest. The loss is not merely a matter of beauty. Artificial light at night confuses migrating birds, which may circle bright buildings until they are exhausted, and it leads newly hatched sea turtles away from the ocean and toward roads and parking lots. Much of this light, moreover, does no one any good: it shines upward or sideways into the sky instead of onto the ground where people walk. Fortunately, the solution is cheaper than for most kinds of pollution. Lamps that point downward and switch off when no one is near save energy and bring back the dark, and the effect is immediate.
opts: How Birds Find Their Way by the Stars
Light Pollution: What We Lose and How to Fix It
The Life Cycle of Sea Turtles
exp: 밤의 인공조명 때문에 별이 보이지 않고 철새와 새끼 바다거북이 피해를 입으며(잃는 것), 아래를 비추고 저절로 꺼지는 등으로 해결할 수 있다(고치는 법)는 글이다. 새와 거북은 피해의 예일 뿐이고, 가로등을 더 밝게 하자는 것은 글과 반대다.

q:
다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

A search for almost any symptom now returns thousands of pages within a second. Some are written by medical organizations and reviewed by experts; many others are produced by companies with something to sell or by individuals repeating what they have heard. The trouble is that all of them look equally convincing on a screen, and the page that appears first is not necessarily the most reliable. Before acting on health advice found online, readers should ask who wrote it, when it was last updated, and whether it points to evidence. Advice that promises a quick cure, relies on one person's story, or urges you to buy a product deserves particular suspicion. It is also wise to compare what several trustworthy sources say rather than to stop at the first answer. When doubt remains, the question is best taken to a doctor or a pharmacist.
opts: 증상이 있으면 병원에 가기 전에 먼저 인터넷으로 찾아보아야 한다.
인터넷의 건강 정보는 출처와 근거를 확인하고 받아들여야 한다.
의료 기관이 쓴 글은 너무 어려워서 쓸모가 없다.
건강 정보는 빨리 찾을 수 있는 것일수록 믿을 만하다.
exp: 인터넷의 건강 정보는 전문가가 쓴 것과 물건을 팔려는 글이 섞여 있으므로 누가 썼는지, 언제 고쳤는지, 근거가 있는지를 확인하라는 글이다. 먼저 인터넷으로 찾아보라고 권하는 글이 아니고, 의료 기관의 글은 오히려 믿을 만한 쪽으로 제시되며, 맨 먼저 나오는 글이 가장 믿을 만한 것은 아니라고 했다.

q:
다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

When we think of good communicators, we usually picture people who speak well. Yet the most trusted colleagues are often those who listen well. A good listener does not plan a reply while the other person is still talking. Instead, he or she pays full attention, asks questions to check understanding, and waits before giving an opinion. This is harder than it sounds, because most of us are eager to show what we know or to offer a solution at once. People who feel heard, however, are more willing to share problems early, which helps a team prevent small troubles from growing into large ones. They are also more ready to accept advice when it finally comes, since they know it is based on what they actually said. Speaking skills may impress others, but it is careful listening that builds lasting trust.
opts: 신뢰를 쌓는 데에는 말솜씨보다 주의 깊게 듣는 태도가 중요하다.
회의에서는 자신의 의견을 먼저 분명하게 밝혀야 한다.
문제가 생기면 먼저 혼자 해결하려고 노력해야 한다.
말하기 능력은 꾸준히 훈련하면 누구나 기를 수 있다.
exp: 가장 신뢰받는 동료는 말을 잘하는 사람이 아니라 잘 듣는 사람이라는 글이다. 마지막 문장의 "it is careful listening that builds lasting trust"가 요지다. 좋은 청자는 의견을 말하기 전에 기다린다고 했으므로 의견을 먼저 밝히라는 선지는 글과 맞지 않고, 혼자 해결하라는 말이나 말하기 훈련 이야기는 없다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Most people think of dust as nothing more than a nuisance, something to be wiped from shelves and swept out of corners.

(A) These tiny grains do not stay where they started. Strong winds lift them high into the air and can carry them across entire oceans, sometimes for thousands of kilometers.
(B) Yet dust plays an important role in nature. Much of it consists of fine grains of minerals blown up from dry land such as deserts and empty lake beds.
(C) When they finally settle after this long journey, the minerals they contain, such as iron and phosphorus, feed plants on land and tiny organisms in the sea. Dust from the Sahara, for example, is known to fertilize the rainforest of the Amazon.
exp: 먼지를 귀찮은 것으로만 여긴다는 주어진 글 뒤에, Yet으로 먼지의 중요한 역할을 꺼내는 (B)가 온다. (A)의 These tiny grains는 (B)의 광물 알갱이를 가리키고, (C)의 this long journey는 (A)에서 바람에 실려 바다를 건너는 이동을 가리키므로 (B)-(A)-(C)이다. (C)가 (A) 앞에 오면 "이 긴 여행"이 가리킬 내용이 없다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

A patient arriving at an emergency room is not always treated in the order of arrival. Someone who came in an hour ago may still be sitting in the waiting area while a new arrival is taken straight in.

(A) According to this level, those in the most serious condition, such as a person with chest pain or heavy bleeding, are seen immediately, while those with minor problems may wait for hours.
(B) Sorting patients by urgency in this way may seem unfair to people who have waited a long time, but it saves lives by directing limited staff and equipment to where they are needed most.
(C) Instead of following the order of arrival, a nurse first checks each patient's symptoms and vital signs, such as pulse and breathing, and assigns a level of urgency.
exp: 도착 순서대로 진료하지 않는다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 그 대신 간호사가 긴급도를 매긴다는 (C)가 온다. (A)의 this level은 (C)의 a level of urgency를 가리키고, (B)의 "이렇게 긴급도에 따라 환자를 나누는 것"은 (C)와 (A)의 내용 전체를 받아 평가하므로 마지막에 온다. (A)나 (B)가 먼저 오면 this level과 in this way가 가리킬 것이 없다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

In the 1840s, a young doctor working in a large hospital in Vienna noticed something puzzling about its two wards for women giving birth.

(A) Looking for a difference between them, he realized that the doctors and students often came to the mothers straight from examining dead bodies, and he suspected that they were carrying something harmful on their hands.
(B) Far more mothers died of fever in the ward where medical students were trained by doctors than in the ward run by midwives, although both belonged to the same hospital.
(C) So he ordered them to wash their hands in a chlorine solution before seeing patients, and the death rate in their ward dropped sharply. Although many doctors of his day rejected his idea, hand washing is now the first rule of infection control.
exp: 주어진 글의 "이상한 점"이 무엇인지 밝히는 (B)가 먼저 온다(의사 병동의 산모 사망이 훨씬 많음). 두 병동의 차이(a difference between them)를 찾다가 원인을 의사들의 손에서 짐작하는 (A)가 이어지고, 그래서(So) 손을 씻게 하자 사망률이 떨어졌다는 (C)가 결론이다. (C)의 So는 (A)의 추측이 앞에 있어야 성립한다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Recycling plastic is more complicated than most people imagine. Dropping a bottle into the right bin is only the beginning of a long and costly process that many items never complete.

(A) Because the washing has to be done so thoroughly, a single dirty item, such as a container still greasy with food, can spoil a whole batch. This is why residents are asked to rinse containers before putting them out.
(B) For one thing, there are many kinds of plastic, each with a different melting point, and they cannot simply be melted together into new material.
(C) The collected items must therefore be sorted by type, partly by machine and partly by hand, and washed before processing, which takes a great deal of time and money.
exp: 재활용이 복잡하다는 주어진 글 뒤에 첫 번째 이유(For one thing)로 플라스틱 종류가 많아 함께 녹일 수 없다는 (B)가 온다. 그래서(therefore) 종류별로 나누고 씻어야 한다는 (C)가 이어지고, (A)의 the washing은 (C)에서 말한 세척을 가리키므로 마지막에 온다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Smallpox was once among the most feared diseases in the world. It killed a large share of those who caught it and left many survivors with deep scars.

(A) He tested this idea in 1796 by scratching material from a cowpox sore into the arm of a young boy and later exposing him to smallpox; the boy stayed healthy.
(B) An English doctor named Edward Jenner noticed, however, that milkmaids who had caught cowpox, a mild disease of cattle, did not seem to get smallpox. He guessed that cowpox somehow protected them.
(C) This method, which came to be called vaccination, spread around the world, and in 1980 smallpox was declared wiped out, the first human disease ever to be eliminated in this way.

* smallpox: 천연두  * cowpox: 우두
exp: 천연두가 무서운 병이었다는 주어진 글 뒤에, however로 제너의 관찰과 추측을 소개하는 (B)가 온다. (A)의 this idea는 (B)의 "우두가 보호해 준다"는 추측을 가리키고, (C)의 This method는 (A)에서 한 접종을 가리키므로 (B)-(A)-(C)이다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

When you step outside on a freezing day, your body immediately begins working to protect its vital organs. It does so in stages, saving its strongest measure for last.

(A) If this first response is still not enough to keep the core warm, the muscles start to contract rapidly, a reaction we know as shivering, which produces heat but uses up a great deal of energy.
(B) First, the blood vessels near the skin become narrower, so that less warm blood flows to the surface and less heat escapes into the air.
(C) That is why your fingers and ears, which now receive less blood, turn pale and feel cold long before the rest of you does. For the same reason, they are the first parts to be injured by extreme cold.
exp: 몸이 단계적으로 반응한다는 주어진 글 뒤에 First로 첫 반응(혈관 수축)을 말하는 (B)가 온다. (C)의 That is why와 "이제 피를 덜 받는"은 (B)의 내용을 바로 받는다. (A)는 이 첫 반응으로 부족할 때 일어나는 다음 반응(떨림)이므로 마지막에 온다. (A)가 (C) 앞에 오면 That이 떨림을 가리키게 되어 맞지 않는다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Last winter, Minho lost his wallet on a crowded bus on his way home from work. He did not notice until he reached his front door and put his hand in his pocket.

(A) The next morning, however, his phone rang, and an unfamiliar voice asked whether he had lost something on the bus the day before.
(B) The caller turned out to be a high school student who had found the wallet under a seat and had seen his business card inside. When they met that afternoon, nothing was missing, and the student would accept no reward but a word of thanks.
(C) He searched his coat and bag again and again that evening, called the bus company without success, and finally gave up, sure that he would never see it again.
exp: 지갑을 잃어버렸다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 그날 저녁 찾다가 포기했다는 (C)가 온다. 그런데(however) 다음 날 아침 전화가 왔다는 (A)가 이어지고, 그 전화를 건 사람(The caller)이 누구였는지와 그날 오후의 만남을 말하는 (B)가 마지막이다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Almost everyone has shed tears while chopping an onion, even when there was nothing to be sad about. An onion does not affect the eyes until it is cut, so what happens at that moment?

(A) The cause is a gas that is released when the knife breaks the onion's cells. The gas rises from the cutting board, and when it reaches the eyes, it irritates their sensitive surface.
(B) These tears can be reduced, however, by chilling the onion before cutting it, since the cold slows the release of the gas. Using a sharp knife also helps, because it damages fewer cells than a dull one.
(C) To wash this irritating substance away, the eyes produce tears, just as they do when dust or smoke gets into them.
exp: 양파를 썰 때 눈물이 난다는 주어진 글 뒤에 그 원인(The cause)인 기체를 설명하는 (A)가 온다. (C)의 this irritating substance는 (A)의 기체를 가리키며 그것을 씻어 내려고 눈물이 난다고 하고, 이 눈물(These tears)을 줄이는 방법을 말하는 (B)가 마지막이다. (B)의 the gas도 (A)에서 먼저 소개되어야 한다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

At regular intervals, usually every five or ten years, most governments count everyone living in the country in a survey known as a census. The practice is very old, but its purpose has grown far beyond the original aims of collecting taxes and finding soldiers.

(A) Since such decisions depend on the results, residents are urged to answer every question accurately. In return, the law usually requires that individual answers be kept secret and used only for statistics.
(B) With these detailed answers in hand, officials can see how the population is changing and decide where new schools, hospitals, and roads will be needed in the years ahead.
(C) The count is not limited to the number of people. Households are also asked about matters such as age, occupation, education, and the kind of housing they live in.

* census: 인구 조사
exp: 인구 조사를 소개한 주어진 글 뒤에, 사람 수만 세는 것이 아니라 여러 가지를 묻는다는 (C)가 온다. (B)의 these detailed answers는 (C)의 질문에 대한 답을 가리키고, (A)의 such decisions는 (B)에서 말한 학교·병원·도로에 관한 결정을 가리키므로 (C)-(B)-(A)이다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

It is widely believed that the color red makes bulls angry. The belief is easy to understand, since the cape that a bullfighter holds out to the bull is traditionally bright red.

(A) What provokes the animal, then, is not the color of the cape but the way the bullfighter waves it sharply back and forth.
(B) In fact, however, cattle cannot see red as a distinct color. Like many other mammals, they have eyes that are poor at telling red from green, so a red cape does not stand out to them as it does to us.
(C) Movement seems to have the same effect outside the bullring: bulls are said to charge at a waving cloth of any color and to pay little attention to a red one that is kept still.
exp: 빨간색이 소를 화나게 한다는 통념 뒤에, however로 소는 빨간색을 구별하지 못한다고 반박하는 (B)가 온다. 그렇다면(then) 소를 자극하는 것은 색이 아니라 천의 움직임이라는 (A)가 이어지고, 투우장 밖에서도 움직임이 같은 효과(the same effect)를 내는 것으로 보인다는 (C)가 마지막이다. (C)는 움직임 이야기가 먼저 나온 (A) 뒤에만 올 수 있다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

That result was a forest floor piled high with dead branches and dry leaves, which small, regular fires would once have burned away.

For many decades, parks in the region put out every forest fire as quickly as possible. (A) Managers believed that fire only destroyed and that a healthy forest was one that never burned. (B) Over time, however, this policy produced an unexpected result. (C) When a fire finally did break out in a dry summer, this thick layer of fuel made it far larger and hotter than any natural fire, and even old trees that had survived many smaller fires were killed. (D) Having learned this lesson, managers today deliberately set small, controlled fires in cool, damp weather to clear away the fuel before it becomes dangerous. Some kinds of pine, they have also found, actually depend on occasional fire, because their cones stay tightly closed until the heat of a fire opens them and releases the seeds.
exp: 주어진 문장은 불을 모두 끈 결과 마른 가지와 잎이 쌓였다는 내용이다. That result는 (B) 뒤 문장의 an unexpected result를 받아 그것을 구체적으로 풀어 주므로 그 문장보다 앞에 올 수 없고, (C) 뒤의 this thick layer of fuel이 바로 이 쌓인 가지와 잎을 가리키므로 (C)에 들어가야 한다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

For example, a nurse may notice that a patient is breathing a little faster than an hour ago.

Machines in a modern hospital monitor patients around the clock, recording heart rate, blood pressure, and oxygen levels every few seconds. (A) Yet experienced nurses often detect trouble before any alarm sounds. (B) Such a small change may not be enough to trigger a monitor, which is set to react only when a figure crosses a fixed line, but it can be the first sign of a serious problem. (C) By reporting it early, the nurse gives doctors time to act before the patient's condition grows worse. (D) Some hospitals now encourage nurses to call for help on the strength of such concern alone, even when every number on the screen looks normal. Technology is valuable, but it cannot replace the trained eye of a person at the bedside.
exp: 주어진 문장은 경험 많은 간호사가 경보보다 먼저 이상을 알아챈다는 말의 예(For example)이므로 그 문장 뒤인 (B)에 온다. 바로 뒤의 Such a small change가 "호흡이 조금 빨라진 것"을 가리킨다는 점도 단서다. (C)나 (D)에 넣으면 Such a small change와 it이 가리킬 내용이 앞에 없게 된다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

It continues to follow the time at home, so you feel sleepy at noon and wide awake at midnight.

When you fly across several time zones, your body clock does not reset at once. (A) Fortunately, there are ways to help it adjust to the new schedule. (B) Light is the most powerful signal for resetting the clock, so spending time outdoors in daylight is especially useful during the first days after arrival. (C) Eating meals at local times and avoiding long daytime naps also speed up the adjustment, since they tell the body when the day begins and ends. (D) Even so, most travelers need several days to recover completely, and the more time zones they have crossed, the longer it takes. Many people also find that flying east, which shortens the day, is harder on the body than flying west.
exp: 주어진 문장의 It은 첫 문장의 your body clock을 가리키며, 체내 시계가 바로 맞춰지지 않는다는 말을 구체적으로 설명한다. 그 뒤에 Fortunately로 해결 방법이 이어지므로 (A)가 알맞다. (B) 이후는 모두 적응을 돕는 방법과 회복 기간이어서 증상을 말하는 문장이 들어갈 수 없다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

Unlike the warning signs, this playful idea worked.

A small town wanted to reduce litter in its central park, where wrappers and paper cups were left on the grass every weekend. (A) At first, officials put up signs warning that anyone caught littering would be fined. (B) Few people were ever caught, however, and the park remained as dirty as before. (C) Then the town tried a different approach: it painted bright green footprints on the ground leading to each trash can. (D) Within weeks, the amount of litter had fallen noticeably, without a single fine being issued. Children in particular enjoyed following the footprints, and their parents followed them. The experience suggests that people do not always need to be threatened into behaving well. Sometimes it is enough to make the right action easy to notice and a little bit fun.
exp: 주어진 문장의 this playful idea는 쓰레기통으로 이어지는 초록 발자국을 그린 일을 가리키므로 그 내용이 나온 뒤인 (D)에 와야 한다. 효과가 있었다(worked)는 말 뒤에 쓰레기가 눈에 띄게 줄었다는 구체적인 결과가 이어진다. (C)에 넣으면 발자국 이야기가 아직 나오지 않아 this playful idea가 가리킬 것이 없다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

The reason lies in the way the two materials conduct heat.

Touch a metal spoon and a wooden spoon that have been lying in the same drawer overnight. (A) The metal one will feel distinctly colder. (B) Yet both are at exactly the same temperature as the room, so why do they feel different? (C) Metal is a good conductor and carries heat away from your fingers quickly, while wood, a poor conductor, does so very slowly. (D) What your skin senses, therefore, is not the temperature of the object itself but how fast heat is leaving your hand. The same principle explains why a tiled bathroom floor feels colder to bare feet than a rug in the same room, and why a metal bench in winter seems far icier than a wooden one. It also explains why pots are made of metal while their handles are often made of wood or plastic.
exp: 주어진 문장의 The reason은 "온도가 같은데도 왜 다르게 느껴지는가"라는 물음의 답을 꺼내는 말이므로, 그 물음 바로 뒤인 (C)에 와야 한다. 바로 뒤에 금속과 나무가 열을 전하는 방식의 차이가 구체적으로 이어진다. (B)에 넣으면 Yet으로 시작하는 문장이 앞 문장과 대조를 이루지 못하고, (D)에 넣으면 열전도 차이를 이미 설명한 뒤여서 같은 말을 되풀이하게 된다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

This, however, is exactly the wrong thing to do.

Nosebleeds are common, especially in dry winter air, and are usually harmless. (A) When one starts, many people tilt their head back to keep the blood from dripping onto their clothes. (B) The reason is that, with the head back, the blood runs down the throat into the stomach, where it can cause nausea and vomiting. (C) Instead, you should sit up, lean slightly forward, and pinch the soft part of your nose firmly for about ten minutes, breathing through your mouth. (D) Resist the temptation to let go every minute to check, since the pressure must be continuous to work. If the bleeding still has not stopped after a second try, or if it follows a blow to the head, you should see a doctor.
exp: 주어진 문장의 This는 고개를 뒤로 젖히는 행동을 가리키므로 그 내용이 나온 뒤인 (B)에 와야 한다. 바로 뒤의 The reason is ~가 왜 잘못인지(피가 목으로 넘어가 메스꺼움을 일으킴)를 설명하고, (C) 뒤의 Instead는 올바른 방법을 소개한다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

Even so, the apps cannot be relied on for every conversation.

Translation apps have become a familiar sight in hospitals that treat foreign patients. (A) A nurse speaks into a phone, and a moment later the patient hears the question in his or her own language. (B) For simple matters such as meal times or directions to the X-ray room, the apps work well enough. (C) They are also available at any hour, unlike human interpreters, who must usually be booked in advance. (D) When a doctor has to explain a diagnosis or obtain consent for surgery, a small error in translation could have serious consequences, so a trained medical interpreter is still called in. An interpreter can also notice when a patient looks confused and ask the doctor to explain again, which no app can do.
exp: 주어진 문장은 Even so(그렇다 하더라도)로 앞에 나온 번역 앱의 장점들과 반대되는 한계를 꺼낸다. (D) 앞까지는 장점(간단한 일에 쓸 만함, 언제든 쓸 수 있음)이 이어지고, (D) 뒤는 진단 설명이나 수술 동의에는 전문 통역사를 부른다는 한계의 구체적인 내용이므로 (D)가 알맞다. (C)에 넣으면 뒤 문장의 also가 이어지지 않는다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

The rest lies hidden beneath the water, where it may extend far out to the sides.

Only about one-tenth of an iceberg can be seen above the surface of the sea. (A) A ship that keeps clear of the visible ice may therefore still strike the part it cannot see. (B) To reduce this danger, an international patrol has been tracking icebergs in the North Atlantic since shortly after the Titanic sank in 1912. (C) In its early years the patrol relied on ships that searched the foggy shipping lanes; today, aircraft and satellites do much of this work, and warnings are sent to ships every day. (D) Thanks to these efforts, collisions with icebergs have become rare. Even so, captains are still advised to slow down and keep a careful watch whenever they pass through waters where ice has been reported.
exp: 주어진 문장의 The rest는 첫 문장의 "10분의 1"을 뺀 나머지를 가리키므로 첫 문장 바로 뒤인 (A)에 와야 한다. 그 뒤 문장의 therefore와 "보이지 않는 부분"도 나머지가 물속에서 옆으로 뻗어 있다는 말이 먼저 나와야 이어진다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

But in soil that is kept constantly wet in this way, the roots are starved of air and begin to rot.

More houseplants die from too much water than from too little. (A) Owners who see a drooping leaf often assume that the plant is thirsty and water it again. (B) A plant with rotting roots can no longer take up water, so its leaves droop even more, and the owner adds yet more water. (C) The way out of this cycle is to check the soil, not the leaves. (D) If the top few centimeters feel dry to the finger, it is time to water; if not, wait. It also helps to use a pot with holes in the bottom, so that extra water can drain away instead of collecting around the roots. Most plants recover from a few dry days far more easily than from a week of standing in water.
exp: 주어진 문장의 in this way는 잎이 처질 때마다 물을 또 주는 행동을 가리키므로 그 문장 뒤인 (B)에 와야 한다. 바로 뒤의 "뿌리가 썩은 식물"은 주어진 문장에서 뿌리가 썩기 시작한다는 말이 먼저 나와야 이어진다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

To end this confusion, the railroads of the United States and Canada agreed in 1883 to divide the continent into a small number of time zones.

Until the nineteenth century, every town kept its own time. (A) Noon was simply the moment when the sun stood highest in the sky, so a clock in one town might differ by several minutes from a clock in the next town to the east or west. (B) As long as people traveled on foot or by horse, these small differences did not matter. (C) The spread of the railroad, however, changed the situation, for a traveler crossing the country passed through dozens of local times, and timetables became almost impossible to read. (D) Within each zone, all clocks showed the same hour, whatever the position of the sun. The following year, an international conference chose the line passing through Greenwich, England, as the starting point for measuring time around the world.
exp: 주어진 문장의 this confusion은 (D) 앞 문장에서 말한, 지역 시간이 수십 개여서 열차 시간표를 읽기 어려웠던 혼란을 가리킨다. 또 (D) 뒤의 Within each zone은 주어진 문장의 time zones가 먼저 나와야 이어지므로 (D)가 알맞다. (C)에 넣으면 철도 때문에 생긴 혼란이 아직 나오지 않았고, 뒤 문장의 however가 가리키는 흐름도 끊긴다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Walking is one of the easiest forms of exercise to begin, which is why doctors so often recommend it to people who have not been active for years. (A) It requires no special equipment other than a comfortable pair of shoes, and it can be done almost anywhere and at any time of day. (B) A brisk thirty-minute walk each day strengthens the heart, helps control weight, and puts far less strain on the knees than running does. (C) The price of running shoes has risen sharply in recent years because of higher material costs. (D) Walking also improves mood, since physical activity triggers the release of chemicals in the brain that reduce stress. Those who find thirty minutes too long can begin with ten and add a little each week, for what matters most is making the walk a daily habit.
exp: 걷기는 시작하기 쉽고 심장, 체중, 기분에 좋다는 글이다. (C)는 신발이라는 낱말로 이어지는 듯하지만 운동화 가격이 올랐다는 내용이어서 걷기의 장점이라는 흐름에서 벗어난다. (A)는 준비물이 거의 필요 없다는 점, (B)와 (D)는 몸과 기분에 주는 효과를 말한다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

More and more government services are moving online. (A) Citizens can now obtain many certificates at home, at any hour, without visiting an office or waiting for it to open. (B) This saves travel time and shortens the lines for those who still need to come in person. (C) Some older residents, however, find the websites difficult to use, so offices keep staff available to assist them and offer classes on how to use the services. (D) Many young people today prefer shopping online to visiting stores, and delivery has become faster every year. People without a computer or a smartphone must not be forgotten either, which is why paper forms and telephone service are still provided. Making services digital while leaving no one behind remains the goal.
exp: 행정 서비스의 온라인화가 주는 편리함과, 이용이 어려운 주민에 대한 배려를 다룬 글이다. (D)는 젊은 층의 온라인 쇼핑과 배송 이야기여서 행정 서비스와 관계가 없다. (C)는 however로 온라인 이용이 어려운 주민 문제를 꺼내고, 그 뒤의 문장이 either로 이를 이어받는다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Blood for transfusion cannot be manufactured; it can only come from volunteers who are willing to give it. (A) A person's blood type is determined by genes inherited from his or her parents, just as eye color is. (B) Because blood components can be stored for only a limited time, in some cases no more than a few days, hospitals need a steady supply throughout the year. (C) Supplies tend to fall during holidays and in winter, when fewer people come to donate, although accidents and operations do not stop. (D) For this reason, blood centers run special campaigns at these times to encourage donors, sending buses to schools, offices, and military bases. Giving blood takes about an hour in all, and the body replaces the lost fluid within a day or two.
exp: 혈액은 헌혈로만 얻을 수 있고 오래 보관할 수 없어 꾸준한 공급이 필요하다는 글이다. (A)는 혈액형이 유전으로 정해진다는 내용이어서 헌혈과 혈액 수급이라는 흐름과 관계가 없다. (D)의 these times는 (C)의 연휴와 겨울을 가리킨다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Noise is often regarded as a mere annoyance, but a growing body of research indicates that it can harm health. (A) Studies have linked living near airports or busy roads with higher rates of high blood pressure and heart disease. (B) Airports have become important centers of trade as air travel has grown, and many cities compete to attract new routes. (C) Even when noise does not wake us, it can raise the level of stress hormones during sleep, so that the body never rests completely. (D) Children in noisy schools have also been reported to learn to read more slowly than those in quiet ones. In response, some cities now build sound barriers along highways, limit night flights, and require better windows in homes near busy roads. Quiet, it seems, is not a luxury but a part of public health.
exp: 소음이 고혈압, 심장병, 스트레스 호르몬, 아이들의 학습에 나쁜 영향을 준다는 글이다. (B)는 공항이라는 낱말이 겹치지만 공항이 무역의 중심지가 되었다는 내용이어서 소음과 건강이라는 주제에서 벗어난다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Reading aloud to young children brings benefits that last for years. (A) Many children's books are printed on thick paper so that they are not easily torn by small hands. (B) Children who are read to regularly hear many more words than those who are not, including words that rarely come up in everyday conversation, and their vocabulary grows faster. (C) They also learn to sit still and follow a story from beginning to end, a skill that helps them when they enter school. (D) Just as important, the shared time strengthens the bond between parent and child, since the child has the adult's full attention. Experts add that it is not necessary to read for long: ten or fifteen minutes at bedtime every night is worth more than an hour once a week.
exp: 아이에게 책을 읽어 주면 어휘력, 집중해서 이야기를 따라가는 힘, 부모와의 유대가 자란다는 글이다. (A)는 어린이 책의 종이 두께에 관한 내용이어서 책 읽어 주기의 효과와 관계가 없다. (C)의 They는 (B)의 "책을 읽어 주는 것을 듣는 아이들"을 가리켜 (B)와 이어진다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Sunscreen works only when it is used properly, and many people do not use it that way. (A) It should be applied about fifteen to thirty minutes before going outdoors so that it has time to settle on the skin. (B) Most people use far too little; an adult needs roughly a shot glass of lotion to cover the whole body, and places such as the ears, the back of the neck, and the tops of the feet are often missed. (C) Tanned skin was once regarded as a sign of outdoor labor, but it later became fashionable among city dwellers. (D) Because sweat and water wash the lotion away, it must be put on again every two hours and after swimming. Sunscreen is needed on cloudy days as well, since much of the sun's ultraviolet light passes through clouds.
exp: 자외선 차단제를 제대로 쓰는 방법(바르는 때, 양, 덧바르기, 흐린 날)을 설명하는 글이다. (C)는 햇볕에 그을린 피부에 대한 인식이 바뀌었다는 내용이어서 차단제의 올바른 사용법이라는 흐름에서 벗어난다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Emergency call centers receive many calls that are not emergencies at all. (A) People call to ask about bus schedules, to complain about noisy neighbors, or even to request help opening a locked door. (B) Mobile phones have replaced public telephones on most city streets, and few children today have ever used a phone booth. (C) Each needless call occupies an operator who might otherwise be answering someone in real danger, and in a fire or a heart attack a delay of even one minute can matter. (D) To keep the emergency line free, many cities have set up a separate number for everyday questions and complaints. Public campaigns also teach residents when to use each number: the emergency line when life or property is in immediate danger, and the other line for everything else.
exp: 긴급 전화에 긴급하지 않은 전화가 많이 걸려 와 정작 위급한 사람의 전화를 받지 못할 수 있고, 그래서 따로 민원 번호를 둔다는 글이다. (B)는 전화라는 낱말로 이어지는 듯하지만 휴대 전화가 공중전화를 대신하게 되었다는 내용이어서 흐름과 관계가 없다. (C)의 Each needless call은 (A)에서 든 전화들을 받는다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Caffeine does not give the body new energy; it only hides tiredness. (A) It works by blocking a chemical in the brain that builds up during the day and makes us feel sleepy. (B) When the caffeine wears off, the tiredness that was hidden returns, often all at once, which is why many people reach for a second or third cup. (C) Moreover, since caffeine stays in the body for many hours, a cup in the late afternoon can still disturb sleep at night, leaving us even more tired the next morning. (D) Coffee beans are grown mainly in warm regions near the equator and are shipped all over the world. A short nap or an earlier bedtime is a far better answer to tiredness than another cup.
exp: 카페인은 피로를 없애는 것이 아니라 가릴 뿐이고 밤잠까지 방해하므로, 피곤하면 자는 것이 낫다는 글이다. (D)는 커피콩의 재배 지역과 수출에 관한 내용이어서 카페인과 피로라는 흐름에서 벗어난다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

A school nurse does far more than put bandages on scraped knees. (A) Nursing uniforms have changed a great deal over the past hundred years, from long dresses and caps to simple, practical clothing. (B) The nurse looks after students with long-term conditions such as asthma or diabetes, making sure they take their medicine on time and know what to do if they feel unwell. (C) He or she also checks students' eyesight and hearing, so that problems are found before they affect learning. (D) When an infectious disease appears in a class, it is the nurse who reports it and advises teachers and parents on what to do. In addition, many school nurses teach lessons on topics such as nutrition, hand washing, and first aid. In all these ways, they help keep children healthy enough to learn.
exp: 보건교사가 만성 질환 학생 돌보기, 시력·청력 검사, 감염병 대응, 보건 교육 등 여러 일을 한다는 글이다. (A)는 간호사 복장의 변화에 관한 내용이어서 보건교사가 하는 일이라는 흐름과 관계가 없다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Staring at a screen for hours tires the eyes, causing dryness, blurred vision, and sometimes headaches. (A) One reason is that we blink far less often than usual when we look at a screen, so the surface of the eye dries out. (B) Eye doctors suggest a simple habit: every twenty minutes, look at something about six meters away for twenty seconds, which lets the muscles that focus the eye relax. (C) Screens have become thinner and lighter every year as technology has advanced. (D) Adjusting the brightness of the screen to match the room and keeping it at arm's length also reduce the strain. So does placing the screen slightly below eye level, because the eyes open less widely when looking down and therefore dry out more slowly. If discomfort continues in spite of these measures, an eye examination is advisable.
exp: 화면을 오래 보면 눈이 피로해지는 이유와 이를 줄이는 방법을 다룬 글이다. (C)는 화면이라는 낱말이 겹치지만 화면이 해마다 얇고 가벼워졌다는 기술 발전 이야기여서 눈의 피로라는 흐름에서 벗어난다. (D)의 also는 (B)의 습관에 이어 또 다른 방법을 더하는 말이다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Many people assume that multitasking helps them get more done. They answer messages during meetings, check the news while writing reports, and feel productive because they are always busy. In fact, the brain cannot focus on two demanding tasks at once; it simply switches rapidly between them. Each switch costs a little time and attention, because the mind must recall where it left off, and the costs add up over a day. In experiments, people who are interrupted by messages typically take longer to finish a piece of writing and make more errors than those who work without interruption. What is more, people who believe they are good at multitasking are not necessarily better at it than anyone else. Doing several things at the same time, in other words, usually means ______.
opts: doing each of them less well
exp: 뇌는 두 가지 일을 동시에 하지 못하고 빠르게 오갈 뿐이며, 그때마다 시간과 주의력이 든다는 글이다. 실험에서도 방해받은 사람들이 더 오래 걸리고 실수가 많았으므로, 여러 일을 한꺼번에 하면 하나하나를 덜 잘하게 된다는 결론이 알맞다. 더 일찍 끝낸다는 선지는 글과 반대다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Placebos are pills that contain no active medicine, yet patients who take them often report feeling better. For a long time this was dismissed as imagination, but researchers now take it seriously. They believe that the improvement comes from ______. When people trust that a treatment will work, the brain can release chemicals of its own that actually reduce pain. Interestingly, studies have reported that the effect tends to be stronger when the pill is larger, when it is described as expensive, or when it is given by a doctor in a white coat who takes time to explain it. Everything that signals serious treatment, it seems, strengthens the patient's belief. This does not mean that placebos can cure infections; their effect is mainly on symptoms such as pain and nausea. Still, it shows that the mind plays a real part in how we feel when we are ill.

* placebo: 위약(가짜 약)
opts: a hidden ingredient in the pills
the patient's expectation of getting well
the low price of the treatment
exp: 빈칸 다음 문장이 "치료가 효과가 있으리라고 믿으면 뇌가 통증을 줄이는 물질을 내보낸다"고 설명하고, 뒤에서도 진지한 치료처럼 보이는 것이 환자의 믿음을 키운다고 했으므로 호전의 원인은 나을 것이라는 환자의 기대다. 위약에는 약 성분이 없다고 했고, 비싸다고 할수록 효과가 크다고 했으므로 나머지 선지는 맞지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Electric cars produce no exhaust gas while they are being driven, so they are often described as perfectly clean. ______, the electricity that charges them may come from power plants that burn coal or gas, and making their batteries requires large amounts of energy and metals such as lithium and cobalt, which must be mined. Part of the pollution, in other words, is not removed but moved from the street to the power plant and the mine. This does not mean that electric cars are worse than gasoline cars; most studies find that they cause less pollution over their whole lifetime. It does mean that how clean they are depends on how the electricity is produced. A country that wants the full benefit of electric cars must therefore clean up its power supply at the same time as it changes what people drive.
exp: 앞 문장은 전기차가 완전히 깨끗하다고들 말한다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 충전용 전기가 석탄·가스 발전소에서 올 수 있고 배터리 생산에도 자원이 많이 든다는 반대 내용이다. 따라서 역접의 However가 알맞다. Therefore는 결과, For example은 예시, Similarly는 비슷한 내용을 이을 때 쓴다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

In a traditional market, prices are rarely fixed. A seller names a price, the buyer offers less, and the two move step by step toward a figure that both can accept. Visitors from countries where bargaining is uncommon often feel uncomfortable with this process. They suspect that they are being cheated, or they pay the first price simply to get away. To the people who shop there every day, however, bargaining is ______. It is a chance to chat, to joke, to ask after each other's families, and to build a relationship that will bring the customer back tomorrow. A seller may add a few extra pieces for a familiar face, and a buyer may accept a slightly higher price from a stall he or she has trusted for years. Seen in this light, the few coins gained or lost matter less than the exchange itself.
opts: a rule set by the government
exp: 빈칸 뒤에서 흥정은 이야기를 나누고 농담을 하고 관계를 쌓는 기회라고 했고, 마지막 문장도 돈보다 주고받는 일 자체가 중요하다고 했으므로 "사회적 교류의 한 형태"가 알맞다. 속는다고 느끼는 것은 흥정이 낯선 방문객의 생각이고, however 뒤에서는 날마다 장을 보는 사람들의 긍정적인 시각이 나온다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Nurses on night shifts must stay alert at hours when the body expects to sleep, and tiredness at such times can lead to errors. Hospitals that have looked into the problem report that short, planned naps are surprisingly effective. A nap of about twenty minutes during a break can restore attention for several hours, whereas a much longer nap may leave a person feeling heavy and slow on waking. Bright lighting in work areas and a light meal instead of a heavy one also help. So does a schedule that avoids too many night shifts in a row and allows enough time to recover between them. Telling tired staff simply to try harder, by contrast, achieves little. These findings suggest that fatigue on the night shift is not just a matter of willpower; it can be ______.
exp: 20분쯤의 계획된 낮잠, 밝은 조명, 가벼운 식사, 무리 없는 근무표가 야간 근무의 피로를 덜어 준다는 글이다. 피로는 의지력만의 문제가 아니라고 했으므로, 세심한 계획으로 관리할 수 있다는 말이 이어져야 한다. 더 노력하라고 말하는 것은 소용이 없다고 했으므로 개인 탓으로 돌린다는 선지는 글과 반대이고, 약 이야기는 없다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

When a new road is built to relieve traffic jams, drivers are usually pleased at first. Journeys that took an hour now take forty minutes. Within a few years, however, the new road is often as crowded as the old one. The reason is that easier driving encourages people to make trips they would not have made before, to move farther from their workplaces, and to give up buses and trains for their cars. Shops and housing also tend to spring up along the new route, bringing still more traffic. Economists call this "induced demand." It explains why cities that keep adding roads rarely solve congestion: ______. For this reason, many planners now argue that money is better spent on public transportation and on bringing homes and workplaces closer together.
opts: new roads cost too much to maintain
more road space attracts more cars
most drivers prefer the older roads
exp: 길이 넓어져 운전이 편해지면 사람들이 차를 더 많이 타게 되어 새 도로도 다시 막힌다는 "유발 수요"를 설명한 글이다. 따라서 도로가 늘면 차도 더 몰린다는 말이 알맞다. 유지비나 옛 도로에 대한 선호는 글에 나오지 않고, 대중교통은 빨라지는 것이 아니라 사람들이 버리는 것으로 나온다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Honeybees cannot speak, but they share information with remarkable precision. When a bee finds a rich patch of flowers, it returns to the hive and performs a dance on the comb, running in a straight line while shaking its body and then circling back to repeat the run. The direction of the straight run shows the direction of the flowers in relation to the sun, and the length of time it lasts indicates how far away they are. Other bees crowd around the dancer and follow its movements closely in the darkness of the hive. They also pick up the scent of the flowers that clings to its body. Then they fly out and are able to find the spot without ever having been there before. Through this dance, a single bee's discovery quickly becomes ______.
opts: a secret kept from the other bees
a serious danger to the queen
a reason to leave the hive for good
knowledge shared by the whole hive
exp: 꿀벌은 춤으로 꽃이 있는 방향과 거리를 알리고, 다른 벌들이 그것을 따라 한 뒤 가 본 적 없는 그곳을 찾아간다는 글이다. 따라서 한 마리의 발견이 벌집 전체가 함께 아는 지식이 된다는 말이 알맞다. 첫 문장의 "정보를 공유한다"와도 이어진다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Many offices have removed walls so that employees can work in one large open room. The idea is that people who can see one another will talk more and share ideas freely. Some studies, however, have found the opposite result. Surrounded by noise and aware of being watched, workers in open offices put on headphones and send messages instead of speaking. In the offices studied, face-to-face conversation actually decreased after the walls came down, while the number of emails and instant messages rose. People seem to need a certain amount of privacy before they feel free to speak openly, and when a room takes that privacy away, they build invisible walls of their own. An office designed to bring people together may, ironically, ______.
opts: make them talk far too much
lower the cost of renting space
exp: 벽을 없앤 사무실에서 오히려 직원들이 헤드폰을 쓰고 메시지로만 소통해 대면 대화가 줄었다는 글이다. ironically(역설적으로)로 보아 사람들을 모으려던 설계가 도리어 서로를 멀어지게 한다는 말이 알맞다. 말을 너무 많이 하게 한다는 선지는 글과 반대다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Vaccines protect not only the people who receive them. When most members of a community are immune to a disease, the germ has difficulty finding a new person to infect, and outbreaks die out quickly instead of spreading. This matters greatly to those who cannot be vaccinated, such as newborn babies who are still too young and people whose immune systems are weakened by illness or treatment. They are shielded because the people around them cannot pass the disease on. The protection weakens, however, when the share of vaccinated people falls. For a highly contagious disease such as measles, nearly everyone must be immune to keep the germ from spreading, and even a small drop can allow it to return. Getting vaccinated, therefore, is not just a personal choice; it is also ______.

* measles: 홍역
opts: a way of protecting one's neighbors
a cure for those already ill
exp: 공동체의 대부분이 면역을 가지면 병이 퍼지지 못해, 접종을 받을 수 없는 신생아나 면역이 약한 사람도 보호받는다는 글이다. 따라서 접종은 개인의 선택일 뿐 아니라 이웃을 지키는 길이라는 말이 알맞다. 신생아에게 위험하다는 것은 글과 반대이고, 치료 이야기는 나오지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

In the first half of the nineteenth century, cities such as London had no modern sewer system, and human waste often flowed into the same rivers from which people drew their drinking water. ______, diseases like cholera spread quickly and killed thousands of people in a single outbreak. At the time, most doctors blamed the foul smell of the air, not the water. It was only when a London doctor, John Snow, marked the homes of the dead on a map in 1854 and found them gathered around a single street pump that suspicion began to turn to the water supply. In the following decades, engineers built underground sewers and cities began to treat their water, and the death rate fell. Clean water and sewers are often said to have saved more lives than any medicine.

* sewer: 하수도
exp: 앞 문장은 오물이 식수를 얻는 강으로 흘러들었다는 원인이고, 뒤 문장은 콜레라가 퍼져 수천 명이 죽었다는 결과이므로 As a result가 알맞다. In contrast는 대조, Nevertheless는 "그럼에도 불구하고", Otherwise는 "그렇지 않으면"이어서 원인과 결과를 잇지 못한다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

People tend to stay with whatever option is already chosen for them. A well-known example comes from retirement savings plans at companies. Where new employees had to fill out a form in order to join the plan, many never got around to it, even though joining was clearly to their advantage. When the rule was changed so that employees were enrolled automatically unless they asked to leave, the great majority stayed in the plan. Nothing else had changed: the plan, the pay, and the kind of workers were the same, and everyone remained free to choose either way. Similar results have been reported for decisions as different as organ donation and the choice of an electricity supplier. Such examples show that ______ can have a powerful effect on what people end up doing.
opts: what is set as the starting option
exp: 가입하려면 서류를 내야 할 때는 많은 사람이 가입하지 않았지만, 자동으로 가입되고 원하면 빠지게 하자 대부분이 남았다는 예다. 달라진 것은 처음에 정해 둔 선택지뿐이므로 그것이 사람들의 행동에 큰 영향을 준다는 말이 알맞다. 첫 문장의 "이미 골라져 있는 선택지에 머문다"와도 맞는다. 급여와 직원은 그대로였다고 했으므로 나머지는 맞지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

If you collapse on a busy street, you might expect that the large number of passers-by guarantees quick help. Psychologists have found that this is not always so. When many people witness an emergency, each one tends to assume that someone else has already called for help or is better able to act. Each also looks at the others, sees that no one is moving, and concludes that the situation may not be serious after all. Responsibility is spread so thinly that no one feels it. A person who is the only witness, by contrast, knows that if he or she does nothing, nothing will be done. For this reason, first-aid instructors teach people not to shout "Somebody call an ambulance!" but to ______.
opts: wait quietly until a doctor passes by
point at one person and tell that person to call
move the patient to a quieter street
ask the whole crowd to step back
exp: 보는 사람이 많으면 저마다 "다른 누군가가 하겠지"라고 생각해 아무도 책임을 느끼지 않고, 목격자가 혼자일 때는 자기가 해야 한다는 것을 안다는 글이다. 그래서 막연히 "누가 좀"이라고 외치지 말고 한 사람을 지목해 책임을 분명히 주라는 말이 알맞다. 나머지는 책임이 흩어지는 문제를 풀어 주지 못한다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Give a student a week to write a short essay, and it will take a week. Give the same student one evening, and the essay will be finished by midnight, often with little difference in quality. Work has a way of expanding to fill the time allowed for it. When time is plentiful, we check our messages, rearrange our notes, and polish details that do not matter, and we tell ourselves that there is no need to begin yet. A tight but realistic limit forces us to decide what is essential and to leave the rest. This does not mean that every job should be rushed; a limit that cannot be met only produces careless work and anxiety. But if you want a task done efficiently, the best thing you can do is to ______.
opts: set a shorter deadline for it
allow as much time as possible
exp: 일은 주어진 시간을 다 채우도록 늘어나고, 빠듯하지만 현실적인 기한이 있어야 꼭 필요한 것에 집중하게 된다는 글이다. 따라서 일을 효율적으로 하려면 기한을 짧게 잡으라는 말이 알맞다. 시간을 넉넉히 주거나 세부를 다듬는 것은 글에서 비효율의 원인으로 든 것이고, 여럿이 나누는 이야기는 없다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

A fever is unpleasant, and many parents rush to bring it down the moment a child feels warm. Yet a fever is not an illness in itself. It is ______: when viruses or bacteria enter, the body raises its own temperature because many germs multiply less well in the heat and the immune system works faster. For this reason, doctors often advise that a mild fever in an otherwise comfortable child need not be treated at once. Medicine may be given to help the child rest or drink, but the aim is comfort, not a particular number on the thermometer. What matters more is how the child looks and behaves, and whether he or she is drinking enough. A very young baby with a fever, a fever that lasts several days, or a child who is hard to wake, however, should be seen by a doctor without delay.
opts: a side effect of taking too much medicine
a sign that the immune system has failed
the main cause of most childhood diseases
one of the body's defenses against infection
exp: 빈칸 뒤에서 병원체가 들어오면 몸이 스스로 체온을 올려 병원체의 증식을 막고 면역 작용을 빠르게 한다고 설명하므로, 열은 감염에 맞서는 몸의 방어 수단이라는 말이 알맞다. 열은 그 자체가 병이 아니라고 했으므로 병의 원인이라는 선지는 맞지 않고, 면역이 실패했다는 것은 글과 반대다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Banks and airports once had a separate line in front of each counter, and customers had to guess which one would move fastest. Most now use a single line that feeds all the counters. The average waiting time is about the same, but the experience is very different. In the old system, a customer stuck behind someone with a complicated problem watched people who had arrived later go ahead in other lines, and grew angrier with every minute. In a single line, everyone is served strictly in the order of arrival, and a slow transaction at one counter delays all customers a little instead of a few customers a lot. Although a single line often looks longer and may discourage people at first sight, customers tend to prefer it. People accept waiting far more readily when they feel that ______.
opts: they can change lines at any time
the staff are working in silence
exp: 줄이 여럿일 때는 늦게 온 사람이 먼저 가는 것을 보게 되지만, 한 줄 서기에서는 온 순서대로 차례가 온다는 글이다. 평균 대기 시간은 비슷하다고 했으므로 사람들이 기다림을 받아들이는 이유는 공정하게 대우받는다는 느낌이다. 한 줄 서기에서는 줄을 바꿀 수 없으므로 줄을 바꿀 수 있다는 선지는 맞지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

The green of summer leaves comes from chlorophyll, the substance that plants use to turn sunlight into food. Leaves also contain yellow and orange pigments, the same kind that color carrots and corn, but in summer these are hidden by the much greater amount of green. As the days shorten and the nights grow cool in autumn, trees prepare for winter by ceasing to produce chlorophyll, and what remains in the leaves breaks down. With the green gone, the other colors can at last be seen. Before the leaves fall, the tree also draws useful nutrients back into its branches and trunk, where they are stored until spring. The yellow and orange of an autumn hillside, in other words, are not newly made in the fall; they ______.

* chlorophyll: 엽록소  * pigment: 색소
opts: are carried up from the roots
appear only after the leaves fall
come from the cold night air
exp: 노란색과 주황색 색소는 여름에도 잎에 있었지만 초록색에 가려져 있었고, 가을에 엽록소가 분해되면서 드러난다는 글이다. 가을에 새로 만들어지는 것이 아니라고 했으므로 "처음부터 줄곧 거기에 있었다"는 말이 알맞다. 뿌리에서 올라온다거나 잎이 진 뒤에 나타난다는 내용은 글에 없다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Most students review by reading their notes again and again. The pages soon look familiar, and this familiarity is easily mistaken for knowledge. Recognizing a sentence when it is in front of you, however, is very different from being able to produce it in an examination room. A more effective method is to close the book and try to recall the material: answer practice questions, or explain the topic aloud without looking. The effort of pulling information out of memory strengthens it far more than putting it in once more. It feels harder and less pleasant than rereading, which is one reason students tend to avoid it. Mistakes made along the way are useful, too, because they show exactly what has not yet been learned. In short, the best way to study is ______.
opts: to read the notes one more time
to memorize the pages in order
exp: 노트를 되풀이해 읽으면 익숙해질 뿐이고, 책을 덮고 문제를 풀거나 설명해 보며 기억에서 꺼내는 것이 더 효과적이라는 글이다. 따라서 가장 좋은 공부법은 스스로 시험해 보는 것이다. 다시 읽기는 글이 덜 효과적이라고 한 방법이고, 실수는 오히려 쓸모가 있다고 했다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Suppose you have paid for a ticket to a concert, and on the evening of the performance you feel ill and a heavy rain is falling. Many people would go anyway, reasoning that otherwise the money would be wasted. Yet the money is gone whether they go or not; the only real question is whether an evening in the hall will be more enjoyable than an evening at home. Economists call a cost of this kind, one that has already been paid and cannot be recovered, a "sunk cost," and they point out that it has no bearing on which choice is better from now on. The same error appears on a larger scale when a company keeps pouring funds into a failing project because so much has already been spent on it. A sensible decision, in short, ______.
opts: is based on how much has already been paid
follows what the majority would choose
depends only on future costs and benefits
avoids every possible risk of losing money
exp: 이미 내서 돌려받을 수 없는 돈(매몰 비용)은 가든 안 가든 사라진 것이므로 앞으로 어느 쪽이 더 나은지와 관계가 없다는 글이다. 따라서 현명한 결정은 앞으로의 비용과 이득만 따진다는 말이 알맞다. 이미 낸 돈을 기준으로 삼는 것은 글이 잘못이라고 한 바로 그 생각이고, 다수의 선택이나 위험 회피는 글에 나오지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

We tend to think of the meaning of a word as something fixed, recorded once and for all in the dictionary. The history of English shows otherwise. Several centuries ago, "nice" meant foolish or ignorant, and to call someone nice was no compliment. "Awful" once described something that filled people with awe, so that a great cathedral could be praised as awful. "Girl" could refer to a young child of either sex. None of these changes was decided by a committee or announced on a particular day. Each came about gradually, as speakers began to use the word in slightly new situations and listeners followed them, until the older sense faded from memory. Dictionaries record such shifts after they have happened; they do not cause them. The meaning of a word, then, is ______.
opts: fixed at the moment the word is first written down
decided by the scholars who compile dictionaries
shaped by the way people actually use it over time
kept unchanged as long as its spelling stays the same
exp: nice, awful, girl의 뜻이 누가 정해서가 아니라 사람들이 조금씩 다르게 쓰면서 서서히 바뀌었다는 글이다. 따라서 낱말의 뜻은 사람들이 실제로 쓰는 방식에 따라 시간이 흐르며 만들어진다는 말이 알맞다. 사전은 변화를 뒤에 기록할 뿐 일으키지 않는다고 했으므로 사전 편찬자가 정한다는 선지는 맞지 않고, 뜻이 고정되어 있다는 것은 첫 문장에서 바로잡는 통념이다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Ask people to picture a desert, and most will describe burning sand under a blazing sun. Scientists, however, define a desert by a different measure. A desert is a region that receives very little precipitation, usually less than about 250 millimeters a year, so that few plants can grow there. By this standard, the largest desert on earth is not the Sahara but Antarctica. Although the continent is covered with ice several kilometers thick in places, very little new snow falls on its interior in a year; the ice has simply built up over an immense span of time because almost none of it melts. Cold, dry regions such as the Gobi in Asia, where winter temperatures fall far below freezing, are deserts as well. What makes a place a desert, in other words, is ______.

* precipitation: 강수량
opts: how hot the ground becomes at noon
how far it lies from the nearest sea
how much of its surface is covered with sand
how little rain or snow falls on it
exp: 과학자들은 더위가 아니라 강수량이 아주 적은가로 사막을 정의하며, 그래서 얼음으로 덮인 남극이 지구에서 가장 큰 사막이라는 글이다. 따라서 사막을 사막으로 만드는 것은 비나 눈이 얼마나 적게 내리는가이다. 뜨거운 땅과 모래는 첫 문장에서 든 통념이고, 남극과 고비 사막의 예가 이를 반박한다. 바다에서 떨어진 거리는 글에 나오지 않는다.

q:
sea otter에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

Sea otters spend almost their entire lives in the cold coastal waters of the North Pacific. Unlike whales and seals, they have no thick layer of fat under the skin; instead, they are kept warm by the densest fur of any animal, which traps a layer of air next to the body. To keep this fur working, they spend several hours a day cleaning it. To maintain their body heat, they must also eat about a quarter of their body weight every day, feeding mainly on sea urchins, crabs, and shellfish. They often float on their backs, place a stone on their chest, and strike a shell against it until it cracks open. When they sleep, they wrap themselves in seaweed so that they do not drift away. Their fur was once so highly prized that hunting nearly wiped them out, and they are now protected by law.
opts: They have a thick layer of fat like seals.
They eat about half of their body weight each day.
They sleep on rocks along the shore.
They use stones to open shellfish.
exp: 해달은 배를 위로 하고 떠서 가슴에 돌을 올려놓고 조개를 내리쳐 깬다고 했다. 고래나 물범과 달리 두꺼운 지방층이 없고 촘촘한 털로 체온을 지키며, 하루에 몸무게의 4분의 1쯤을 먹고, 잘 때는 떠내려가지 않도록 물 위에서 해초를 몸에 감는다.

q:
octopus에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

The octopus is one of the most unusual animals in the sea. It has three hearts and blue blood, and because it has no bones, it can squeeze through extremely narrow gaps; the only hard part of its body is a beak resembling that of a parrot. About two-thirds of its nerve cells are located not in its head but in its eight arms, which can taste what they touch. An octopus can also change the color of its skin within a second to match its surroundings and hide from enemies. When this fails, it may release a cloud of dark ink and escape while the attacker cannot see. In aquariums, octopuses have been observed opening jars to reach the food inside. Despite these remarkable abilities, many species live for only one or two years, and the females usually die soon after their eggs hatch.
opts: It has three hearts and red blood.
Most of its nerve cells are in its arms.
It needs several minutes to change its skin color.
Its females live for many years after their eggs hatch.
exp: 문어의 신경 세포는 약 3분의 2가 머리가 아니라 여덟 개의 팔에 있다고 했다. 피는 파란색이고, 피부색은 1초 안에 바꿀 수 있으며, 암컷은 대개 알이 부화한 뒤 곧 죽는다.

q:
vitamin D에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and is therefore essential for strong bones. Children who lack it may develop soft, weak bones, and adults who lack it are more likely to suffer fractures. Unlike most vitamins, it can be produced by the body itself when the skin is exposed to sunlight. Only a few foods, such as oily fish and egg yolks, contain it naturally, which is why it is added to milk and cereals in some countries. People who spend most of the day indoors, as well as older adults, whose skin makes the vitamin less efficiently, are at greater risk of deficiency. In winter, when sunlight is weak, doctors may recommend supplements. More is not always better, however: because the vitamin is stored in body fat, taking very large doses over a long period can be harmful.
opts: Older adults' skin produces it less efficiently.
It is found naturally in most kinds of food.
The body is unable to make it by itself.
Supplements are mainly recommended in summer.
exp: 노인은 피부에서 비타민 D를 만드는 효율이 떨어져 결핍 위험이 크다고 했다. 비타민 D가 자연적으로 들어 있는 음식은 몇 가지뿐이고, 피부가 햇빛을 받으면 몸에서 스스로 만들 수 있으며, 보충제는 햇빛이 약한 겨울에 권한다.

q:
camel에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

Camels are well suited to life in the desert. Contrary to popular belief, their humps store fat, not water; the fat serves as a source of energy when food is scarce, and a hump may shrink and lean to one side after a long journey. A thirsty camel can drink about a hundred liters of water at one time, and it can then go for many days without drinking again. Its body loses very little water, partly because it does not begin to sweat until its body temperature has risen considerably. Long eyelashes and nostrils that can be closed keep out blowing sand, and wide feet prevent the animal from sinking into it. Thick fur on its back shields it from the sun by day and keeps it warm during cold desert nights. For thousands of years, these qualities have made the camel a valuable means of transport across dry regions.
opts: Their humps are filled with water.
Their wide feet keep them from sinking into the sand.
They are unable to close their nostrils.
They must drink water every day.
exp: 넓은 발 덕분에 모래에 빠지지 않는다고 했다. 혹에는 물이 아니라 지방이 들어 있고, 콧구멍을 닫아 모래를 막을 수 있으며, 한 번 물을 마시면 여러 날 동안 마시지 않고 지낼 수 있다.

q:
Dead Sea에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

The Dead Sea in the Middle East is not really a sea but a lake. Its shore is the lowest point on the land surface of the earth, more than 400 meters below sea level. Water flows into the lake but has no way out except by evaporating in the heat, leaving its salt behind. As a result, the water is almost ten times as salty as the ocean, and no fish can live in it, which is how the lake got its name. The salt also makes the water so dense that swimmers float without effort, and visitors like to be photographed reading a newspaper while lying on the surface. In recent decades the lake has been shrinking, largely because much of the water of the Jordan River, its main source, is taken for farming and drinking before it arrives. Its surface now drops by roughly a meter every year.
opts: People float easily in its water.
It lies more than 400 meters above sea level.
Many kinds of fish live in its salty water.
It has been growing larger in recent decades.
exp: 소금 때문에 물의 밀도가 높아 사람이 힘들이지 않고 뜬다고 했다. 호숫가는 해수면보다 400미터 넘게 낮고(below), 물이 너무 짜서 물고기가 살지 못하며, 요르단강의 물이 도중에 쓰여서 호수는 줄어들고 있다.

q:
bamboo에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

Bamboo is not a tree but a kind of grass. Some species are among the fastest-growing plants in the world and can grow close to a meter in a single day under favorable conditions. Its stem is hollow, yet strong enough to be used for building houses, bridges, and furniture in many parts of Asia, and it is light enough to be carried easily. Young shoots are eaten as a vegetable, and the leaves and stems of certain species are the main food of the giant panda. Because bamboo spreads through underground stems, new stalks keep rising after the old ones are cut, so a grove does not need to be replanted after each harvest. Many kinds of bamboo flower very rarely, some only once in several decades, and the plants often die after flowering.
opts: Its young shoots are used as food.
It is classified as a kind of tree.
Its stem is solid and heavy.
Every species flowers once a year.
exp: 어린 순(죽순)은 채소로 먹는다고 했다. 대나무는 나무가 아니라 풀의 한 종류이고, 줄기는 속이 비어 가벼우며, 꽃은 아주 드물게 피어 수십 년에 한 번 피는 종도 있다.
